title: The Forgotten Backup
summary: A web server leaves an old backup where anyone can download it. Inside is a config file with a database password - and that same password opens a shell. One careless tool finishes the job.
story: {{CO}} (made up) runs web3 on 10.10.12.0/24. You start on scout. Somewhere on the web server is a backup archive that was never meant to be public.
goal: Capture the user flag in {{SVCUSER}}'s home folder and the root flag in /root.
skills: web folder listings, downloading and unpacking a backup, finding a password in a config, ssh, sudo -l

hints.text: Scan the server (nmap -sV 10.10.12.30) and look at its web folders. webscan http://10.10.12.30/ tries common names; one folder lists a file you can download.

The backup folder has site-backup.tar.gz. Download it (curl -o), unpack it (tar xzf), and read the config inside - it has a database password. That password also works for the account {{SVCUSER}} over ssh.
After ssh {{SVCUSER}}@10.10.12.30, run sudo -l: you may run {{SUDOBIN}} as root, which reads any file. On this run: {{SUDORUN}}
